chunks: We were told by my father, and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid, may Allah grant them both mercy, that they both said: We were told by Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Himyari, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, who said: We were told by Nadr ibn Shu'ayb, from Abdul-Ghaffar al-Jazi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he mentioned that
the weakened people are of different kinds, which some contradict the other, and that the one among the people of Qibla who is not a Nasib, is a weakened individual.

key_terms.الْمُسْتَضْعَفِينَ: The weakened or those lacking power/authority
key_terms.نَاصِبًا: Nasib; one who bears enmity towards the Ahl al-Bayt

ai.seo_question: What is the definition of the 'weakened' (mustad'afun) in Shia theology and how are they categorized?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Mani al-Akhbar*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the 'weakened' (al-mustad'afin) are not a monolithic group but consist of different types that may contradict each other. Specifically, he identifies a category of those who are from the people of the Qibla (Muslims) but are not 'Nasib' (those who bear enmity towards the Ahl al-Bayt) as being classified as 'weakened'. This distinction highlights the nuanced Shia understanding of political and theological vulnerability, where internal dissent or external pressure can render even committed Muslims 'weak' in the face of divine decree or historical trials.
